simulator_description: This simulator models COVID spread using a stochastic, discrete-time SIR compartment process where each time step draws new infections from a binomial distribution with hazard-based probability p=1-exp(-beta*I/N) and new recoveries from Binomial(I, gamma), updating integer counts (S,I,R) while enforcing nonnegativity and strict population conservation S+I+R=N for each trajectory. It assumes each observed trajectory represents a closed population with fixed N and uses each trajectory’s initial state as the rollout start, which is consistent with how SIR dynamics are typically conditioned on initial prevalence. Parameters (beta, gamma) are calibrated via simulation-based inference (neural posterior estimation) using only training trajectory_id=0 as the observation, with simulator outputs normalized by N and z-scored for stable learning, and multiple rollouts per parameter averaged to match evaluation on mean trajectories; final performance is assessed by comparing predicted mean trajectories (averaged over many stochastic rollouts) against train/val/test trajectories using MSE and related epidemic-shape metrics.
